item.title: Yung Miami Had The Hit. What Happened With His New Album?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Yung Miami’s dismal debut raises questions about why “Spend Dat” listeners did not help Watch Dis.
item.content:encoded:
Yung Miami probably didn’t picture No. 138 when she named her debut solo album Watch Dis, but that is the Billboard 200 entrance being reported for Caresha’s big musical statement. Now comes the uncomfortable question: How did such a successful single lead to such a modest album opening?

Because “Spend Dat” certainly did its job. According to Universal Music’s album announcement, the record earned platinum certification and peaked at No. 17 on the Billboard Hot 100. That is a substantial achievement for somebody trying to establish herself outside City Girls. The invitation went out. Apparently, everybody didn’t stay for dinner.

Several outlets have reported approximately 10,500 opening units, but album equivalent units include streaming activity. So calling that number 10,500 albums “sold” is pretty misleading. We can discuss a disappointing chart entrance, numbers aside.

The album certainly wasn’t short on recognizable guests. Travis Scott, Summer Walker, Quavo, Bryson Tiller, Rick Ross, Trina and Trick Daddy appear across the project. For accuracy, Travis and Summer are album collaborators. The official “Spend Dat” remix features Lil Baby and Kodak Black, while the international version brings in Davido, Shenseea and Vybz Kartel.

That leaves me wondering whether people embraced the song more than the prospect of a full Caresha album. It happens. Knowing every word to one hook does not automatically mean somebody wants 21 tracks. A feature list can get listeners curious, but the repeat button requires a separate commitment.

Still, Hip-Hop’s obsession with declaring somebody finished after one opening week gets exhausting. A low debut deserves scrutiny. It also leaves room for another song to connect, a performance to change perceptions or listeners to discover something they initially overlooked.

My question is what Caresha does next. Which record gets the push? Does she lean into the party music or give the more personal material some attention?

She asked us to watch. The follow through may be more revealing than the opening number.

item.title: Queen Latifah Brings Newark Housing Mission To BET Documentary
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Queen Latifah's Newark housing effort takes center stage in You Can Go Home Again, premiering November 27 on BET.
item.content:encoded:
Queen Latifah‘s effort to build housing in Newark is headed to BET, which set a Friday, November 27 premiere for “You Can Go Home Again.”

The documentary follows the rapper’s return to the New Jersey community that raised her and the years of work behind RISE Living. The mixed-use development includes affordable apartments, with a name that honors her late mother, Rita.

BET announced that the film will air at 10 p.m. Eastern on the Friday after Thanksgiving. Muta’Ali directed it, with Flavor Unit Entertainment and P&G Studios co-producing.

“It’s about my community and the people and places that make us who we are,” Queen Latifah said.

RISE stands for Rita Is Still Everywhere. Latifah’s mother was a schoolteacher, and the film connects that family history with her investment in the neighborhood.

The housing effort predates the documentary announcement by years. Latifah joined Newark Mayor Ras Baraka for an April 2022 groundbreaking after construction had begun that January. Her BlueSugar Corporation worked with Life Assets Development and Gonsosa on the project.

Plans at the time called for 76 homes, including 16 classified as affordable. The rest included market-rate housing. That distinction is part of the project’s design: RISE was planned as a mixed-use development with affordable units within a larger residential community.

The plans also reserved 1,900 square feet on the ground floor for nonprofit organizations. They included a business center, fitness space and electric-vehicle charging stations, along with in-unit laundry and common-area Wi-Fi. Those were features outlined during the 2022 development phase.

The documentary received a first look in Chicago on November 4, when Latifah appeared with childhood friend and project partner Tammy Hammond at the Obama Presidential Center.

It also extends her work with a network where she now has a role beyond the screen. In June, Latifah and LL Cool J joined BET’s first advisory board. Her television and film production business includes Flavor Unit, which she runs with Shakim Compere.

Compere and Loretha Jones served as executive producers on “You Can Go Home Again.” The film follows the housing work alongside Latifah’s early life in Newark.

item.title: What Will Dr. Dre Do With His AI Double Down?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Dr. Dre welcomed tomorrow’s digital possibilities with unshakable confidence.
item.content:encoded:
We already know Dr. Dre loves AI. A recent chat with Ice Cube and Mike Epps has him leaning in harder.

Dr. Dre embraced artificial intelligence over apprehension during an appearance on “Listen & Laugh” with Ice Cube and Mike Epps as he championed its creative potential in music and movies.

The legendary producer offered an enthusiastic endorsement of AI technology that he believes could expand artistic possibilities.

“I am extremely excited about AI, I love it. I love the potential of it, I love the idea of where it could possibly go with music and film.”

Dre’s enthusiasm extended beyond the recording studio and he suggested his former NWA pal could use AI for acting. Maybe a new Friday that has the original characters? I think I see where Dre is headed with this. He dd not say that, FYI.

His focus was on possibility.

Then he said what we knew he’d say.

“It’s just a whole new level of creativity, I think the only people are going to be mad about AI are people that aren’t that creative.” Well, not that last part. I see so many terrible versions of AI that I am not sure this lines up with my views. I do get what Dre is saying.

That statement moved the discussion from what a machine might accomplish to how an artist might respond. Dre might be plotting something, because why else is he going this hard with it?

Also, it is important to note that Dre’s genius and cache in the culture makes him unique in the industry. For the average person, not so much. Also, we really dd not get into any granular details on what sort of AI he was talking. The larger convo is above.

Which applications does he envision? Excitement about AI in music and film can encompass many possibilities, but bro was vague. Was that on purpose? I don’t know.

For now, the clearest takeaway is Dre’s willingness to embrace experimentation. He described AI as another avenue for creativity and showed little patience for the idea that its arrival should automatically inspire anger.

The attention grabber was his assessment of skeptics and they weighed in as expected – in the comments. I am not judging anybody. Creators get there one way or another. We’ll see.

item.title: Icewear Vezzo Expands Detroit Portfolio With Shadow Gallery Building
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Icewear Vezzo and partner Prevail say they now own the full Shadow Gallery building, expanding their footprint in Detroit.
item.content:encoded:
Icewear Vezzo is expanding his Detroit business portfolio after announcing that he and business partner Prevail now own the entire building that houses The Shadow Gallery in Eastern Market.

The deal goes beyond taking a stake in the venue’s operation. Vezzo and Prevail said their ownership covers the full property, which contains several entertainment and event spaces at 1533 Winder Street. No purchase price or financing terms were disclosed with the announcement.

The Shadow Gallery describes itself as an “entertainment complex” with a lounge, rooftop patio, art gallery, live music venue and event space. Its first floor also includes AWAREHOUSE, a concert and event hub, along with a lobby used for rotating pop-up concepts.

The venue says its upstairs gallery carries rotating contemporary art from local and international artists, while AWAREHOUSE handles live shows and private events. The lobby connects the two spaces and has hosted pop-up concepts. That gives the new owners several possible revenue streams under one roof without depending on a single room or event format.

That mix gives the partners a property with several possible uses inside one of Detroit’s best-known commercial districts. The announcement did not include a redevelopment timeline or explain whether the venue’s current programming will change.

For Vezzo, the purchase continues a run of investments tied closely to Detroit. In December 2025, he and fellow rapper Peezy became the first franchise partners in House of Dank’s history at a store on Gratiot Avenue.

“This isn’t a promotion – this is real ownership,” Vezzo said when that partnership was announced. He described the store as a chance to invest in the East Side neighborhood where he grew up.

The rapper has also put money into housing and community work. In September, Vezzo showed several east-side homes he had purchased for young people aging out of foster care and people recovering from addiction.

“Our job is to show them what love is and what a home is,” he said during the neighborhood tour. Vezzo added that he hoped to extend the project across more of the block.

The Shadow Gallery acquisition moves that ownership strategy into Eastern Market and adds a multi-use commercial property to Vezzo’s growing collection of Detroit investments.

item.title: Tyler Perry Joins Keisha Lance Bottoms’ Georgia Transition Team
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Tyler Perry will co-chair Keisha Lance Bottoms' Georgia transition team as the governor-elect prepares to take office.
item.content:encoded:
Tyler Perry will help guide Georgia’s transfer of power after Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms named him co-chair of her transition team.

Variety reports that the filmmaker and studio owner joined the Georgia’s Promise transition operation as Bottoms prepares to take office. The appointment puts one of the state’s most visible entertainment figures inside the group shaping the new administration’s early agenda.

Bottoms won the governor’s race this week and made history as Georgia’s first Black governor. She will also become the first Black woman to serve as a governor anywhere in the United States. AllHipHop covered the victory as results came in.

Perry shares transition leadership with a group drawn from business, public service and civic organizations. The co-chairs include Arthur Blank, former Walgreens Boots Alliance chief Roz Brewer, attorney Jason Carter and former U.S. Senate candidate Michelle Nunn. Georgia Insurance Commissioner John King is serving as the transition’s chief operating officer.

The group is expected to help Bottoms review state agencies, recruit senior staff and turn campaign priorities into plans for the opening months of her administration. Her stated priorities include health care access, criminal justice reform, mental health diversion courts, flood recovery and the rapid growth of data centers across Georgia.

Perry’s place on the team reflects his long footprint in the state. Tyler Perry Studios occupies a large production campus in Atlanta, and his film and television operation has become a major part of Georgia’s entertainment economy. He has also used his platform for relief work and community aid in the region.

Variety also placed the appointment against Perry’s current legal disputes.

The producer faces civil lawsuits accusing him of sexual assault and other misconduct, allegations he has denied. In one of those cases, AllHipHop reported that Perry asked a court to keep private text messages out of public filings.

Transition co-chairs shape the handoff by bringing leaders into the planning process and helping the governor-elect test ideas before inauguration. Perry’s role gives Atlanta’s film and television sector a direct voice in that work.

The transition team is moving ahead as Bottoms prepares for January. More policy advisers and personnel choices are expected as the incoming administration reviews agencies and builds its first governing plan.

item.title: Are Chris Brown And Usher Beefing?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Chris Brown and Usher’s troubled Atlanta concert sparked beef speculation, but the missing duets have no real explanation.
item.content:encoded:
Chris Brown and Usher have Atlanta fans asking whether the real drama on this tour is behind the scenes.

Their November 5 concert with at Mercedes-Benz Stadium has inspired some questions about their relationship. Concertgoers complained about a lengthy wait, a missing joint performance and a show that felt hurried once it finally got moving.

But is this a cold war? It is too early to call. And yet the streets are talking.

Attendees said there were no shared songs between the headliners, a shortened setlist and chatter about a possible disagreement. Nobody has produced evidence establishing a backstage fight, but we know these people can be divas. When two stars sell a joint experience and fans say something is off…oftentimes that means something is off.  

Some of the details were off too.

Although some attendees placed the start around 10 p.m., others say Usher beginning a few minutes after 9 p.m. The venue advertised 7:30 p.m., and Usher’s representatives said the planned start was 8:30 p.m. Those accounts differ, but not the 3-hour rumors we heard. Hmmmm and yet, nothing really defends the beef allegations.

Then came Breezy.

Brown posted a brief message warning people against believing internet chatter. What remains unclear is exactly which claim he was dismissing. Was it the alleged friction? The concert complaints? He did all that and cleared nothing up.

Fans also suggested a midnight curfew explained the quick finish. Nobody has confirmed this and they do not pay me enough for me to go looking.

The disappointment is real. A vegan beef is rumor.

I don’t think there will be any more to this, at least not publicly.

item.title: Offset Won’t Quit Gambling Despite Hesitation About Casinos
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Offset expressed doubts about returning to a casino but said he would keep gambling as his Don Toliver video drew questions at LAX.
item.content:encoded:
Offset expressed hesitation about returning to a casino when TMZ caught up with him at Los Angeles International Airport. Giving up gambling, though, was not part of the plan he described.

The rapper spoke with TMZ on Thursday, November 5, during an exchange about “Every Night,” his collaboration with Don Toliver. Its casino-themed video brought the conversation around to Offset’s own experiences with gambling. He connected the video’s setting to his life.

His casino history this year includes a shooting in Florida, a money dispute in Detroit and a blackjack argument in Paris.

MotorCity Casino Hotel sued him on March 30 over an alleged $100,000 debt tied to a March 2024 visit. The Detroit casino accused him of failing to repay a gambling marker and alleged that the bank account backing it lacked enough money to cover the amount.

The casino’s complaint alleged fraud, breach of contract and violations of Michigan’s bad-check law. It sought twice the alleged unpaid gambling debt plus legal fees.

On September 11, Michigan’s Wayne County Circuit Judge Qiana Denise Lillard directed the casino to apply for a default after Offset failed to respond to the lawsuit.

On April 6, Offset was shot outside the Seminole Hard Rock in Hollywood, Florida. The shooting took place in the valet area. His spokesperson said he was in stable condition the following day, while police described his injuries as non-life-threatening.

Another casino appearance drew attention on October 5, when video showed him arguing at a Paris blackjack table. That episode preceded the release of “Every Night” and its use of casino imagery.

The label announced the Don Toliver collaboration on October 9 as part of the rollout for GMFU.

Offset most recently pointed to November 13 for the album’s release, after his label announced an earlier October 23 date. The project follows his 2025 album KIARI and its expanded edition.

“Every Night” followed the September single “Something I Need.” Jaasu produced the track, which samples Jodeci’s 1995 song “Freek’n You.” Mikey Rare and SheShe Pendleton directed the video that prompted the casino question at LAX.

item.title: D.L. Hughley Recalls Bill Cosby Clash Over N-Word & Panties
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: D.L. Hughley recalls challenging Bill Cosby during a radio clash that executives pulled before the confrontation could ever air.
item.content:encoded:
D.L. Hughley says a tense radio confrontation with Bill Cosby vanished before listeners ever heard it.

The comedian revisited the encounter during a PBS NewsHour “Settle In” segment with Geoff Bennett. Hughley said Cosby arrived at his New York radio show and was dismissive toward co-hosts Jacque Reid and Steve Wilson.

Expecting the interview to go sideways, Hughley joined the conversation.

Cosby challenged Hughley’s use of the N-word. Hughley responded by bringing up the sexual assault allegations that had followed the entertainer.

“No offense, Mr. Cosby, I say [expletive], but I never had a coed wake up with their panties on backwards,” Hughley recalled telling him.

Hughley said Cosby immediately predicted the exchange would never make it to air.

Executives then came downstairs, took the recording and kept the segment from being broadcast. Hughley did not identify the executives or say who ultimately made the decision. He said the tape never resurfaced, and the interview remained buried.

The moment left him with a difficult distinction. Hughley acknowledged that Cosby changed television and widened the space available to Black families on screen. He also rejected the idea that cultural importance should block scrutiny of a powerful person’s conduct.

“Bill wasn’t Cliff,” Hughley said, separating Cosby from the beloved television father he played.

The allegations have also produced civil judgments. In March 2026, a California jury found Cosby liable for sexually assaulting and battering Donna Motsinger in 1972 and awarded her $19.25 million. Cosby’s attorney, Jennifer Bonjean, said an appeal was planned.

That civil verdict was separate from Cosby’s Pennsylvania criminal case.

His 2018 conviction was overturned in 2021 after the state’s highest court ruled that prosecutors had violated an earlier non-prosecution agreement. He was released after serving nearly three years.

Hughley included the radio encounter in his new memoir, Charlie’s Boy, which traces his childhood in South Central Los Angeles, gang involvement, family trauma and later life as a father and comedian.

The Cosby story fit the larger theme Hughley brought to “Settle In”: success may explain how a person gained influence, but it does not erase what that influence was used to protect.

item.title: Coi Leray Sets “MULTI” Album For February And Drops “Spin Back”
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Coi Leray will release her third album, "MULTI," in February after opening the campaign with the new single "Spin Back."
item.content:encoded:
Coi Leray is putting every side of her sound under one title with MULTI, her third studio album and first full-length project since joining Epic Records.

The album is due February 26, 2027, according to Leray’s official site. She opened the campaign Friday with “Spin Back,” a dance-driven single about the pull of returning to a relationship that already ended.

WhoisRodny, JP Beatz and J Roc Stream produced the new track. It leans into the melodic side of Leray’s catalog while keeping enough pace for the dance floor. The release follows her Diplo collaboration “Nothing Into Something” and extends a year that has moved across rap, electronic music and Latin sounds.

MULTI follows Leray’s 2022 debut, “Trendsetter,” and her self-titled 2023 album. Those records established the New Jersey-raised artist as a rapper and singer willing to move between hard drums, pop hooks and club records.

Her 2023 hit “Players” reached the Top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100 and earned a Grammy nomination for Best Rap Performance.

The new title makes that range the album’s organizing idea. The cover presents Leray in 12 portraits, with different looks and expressions arranged as parts of the same artist.

The campaign treats that range as part of her identity, emphasizing confidence, vulnerability, motherhood and freedom from any single sound.

It will also be Leray’s first album since she signed with Epic in 2025. She introduced that chapter with the “What Happened To Forever?” EP, then spent 2026 releasing collaborations and building a wider musical lane. “Better Than Yours,” her record with NBA YoungBoy, reached No. 1 at urban radio in July.

She later joined Eladio Carrión on “Outside” and Diplo on “Nothing Into Something.”

“Spin Back” brings the focus back to her own album. The song’s romantic tension gives the project an emotional starting point, while its production signals that dance music will remain part of the mix.

Preorders are open for signed blue vinyl, standard vinyl and CD editions. Leray’s site also lists the new single alongside the album campaign, making “Spin Back” the first official preview of MULTI before its February release.

item.title: Kim Kardashian Recalls Fearing Her Career Was Over After All’s Fair Reviews
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kim Kardashian says brutal All's Fair reviews briefly made her fear for her career before the cast chose to double down.
item.content:encoded:
Kim Kardashian admitted the first wave of All’s Fair reviews rattled her enough to wonder if she had damaged her acting career for good.

The reality star and entrepreneur is back as divorce lawyer Allura Grant in the Hulu drama’s second season. She said the harsh response to season one briefly left her worried that her veteran co-stars would blame her for the backlash.

“There was a second when I thought, ‘Oh my God, my career is over,'” Kardashian said while promoting the new season.

That fear did not last. Kardashian said Sarah Paulson left her a supportive voicemail that restored her confidence. Her answer after hearing it was simple: “Okay, what do I do? We double down.”

The first season earned a brutal response from critics, but viewers kept watching. The attention helped All’s Fair hold a top spot on Hulu before the series secured a second-season renewal.

That split became part of the show’s story. Critics gave season one a 6 percent score on Rotten Tomatoes. The audience still pushed the series to the top of Hulu’s chart. Kardashian now sees that gap as proof that reviews did not get the final word.

Kardashian also struck a modest note during an appearance on The View.

She said creator Ryan Murphy was “setting me up for success by surrounding me with the best of the best actors.” Naomi Watts rejected the idea that Kardashian hid behind the cast, while Niecy Nash-Betts told her, “You brought your A-game, baby!”

Season two brings back Glenn Close, Paulson, Watts, Teyana Taylor and Nash-Betts. The first three episodes began streaming on Hulu this week, with new installments set to arrive weekly.

Paulson said Kardashian reached another level late in the new season. She pointed to more confidence and humor in the performance. Watts also said Kardashian grew on set and started adding her own lines. Their comments gave Kardashian an answer to the idea that she was only leaning on the ensemble.

The show is even making room for Kardashian to laugh at herself. A new scene has Allura admit she failed the bar exam on her first try, a nod to Kardashian’s own legal path. Kardashian retook California’s bar exam in July after falling short in 2025.

For now, Kardashian is answering the worst reviews of her acting career with another season, a bigger swing and the backing of the women beside her.
